policy_title: Fund 100,000 Apprenticeships by Curbing Poor University Degrees
stated: The Conservative Party will fund 100,000 high-quality apprenticeships for young people by changing the law to close university courses with high dropout rates or poor graduate outcomes, protecting students and taxpayers.

source.quote: Fund 100,000 high-quality apprenticeships for young people, paid for by curbing the number of poor-quality university degrees that leave young people worse off. ...We will fund this by changing the law to close university courses in England with the worst outcomes for their students.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets apprenticeship supply and university course provision, affecting both vocational skills pathways and higher education access/quality for young people.

Apprenticeships are specifically a route into skilled employment; a material expansion of high-quality apprenticeships would plausibly affect job quality, earnings trajectories, and in-work security for the cohort completing them.

A large-scale increase in vocational skills supply (100,000 additional apprenticeships) would plausibly affect aggregate productivity, business investment in skilled labour, and economic opportunity/mobility — indicators explicitly within O13's scope.

membership_note: Three fundamentals earn real verdicts: O7 (the education/skills pathway effect), O4 (the labour-quality and earnings effect for apprentices), and O13 (the aggregate productivity and opportunity effect). Public-finances effects are framed as a reallocation rather than new borrowing, so O12 does not clearly earn a non-negligible verdict without more detail on the fiscal mechanics.
